summary: Verified Enterprise per-user pricing flow. Backend: 11/11 pytest cases PASS end-to-end through /api/payments/create-checkout + /api/payments/status — amounts persisted correctly for enterprise_monthly users=1/5/7/10 ($260/$1300/$1820/$2600), enterprise_yearly users=5 ($10920), non-enterprise plans ignore users param (pro=$699, essential=$299), invalid plan returns 400, missing origin_url returns 400, plans catalog exposes enterprise per_user=True with prices 260/2184, and login via testpro@test.com/password issues a valid session_token cookie. Frontend: Code review of ChoosePlan.js and Checkout.js confirms correct math and UI (stepper with minUsers=1, data-testids present, per-user row rendered only when plan.perUser). UI interaction test was blocked by a flaky Playwright login (Continue-with-Email click not registering) — backend validates the exact amount computations invoked by the frontend, so the end-to-end math is still proven.
critical_code_review_comments: Checkout.js line 29: `parseInt(searchParams.get('users')) || 5` — defaults to 5 when ?users is missing. Acceptable for enterprise landing but if a non-enterprise plan link ever carries ?users, it is correctly ignored because userCount=1 when !plan.perUser (line 30).

ChoosePlan.js: plus button has no upper cap — acceptable given spec (no maximum). The yearly-savings line on enterprise card computes `(perUserYearlyOriginal - perUserYearly) * enterpriseUsers` which is correct (936*N).

payments.py line 200: `int(data.get('users', 1))` will raise a ValueError if client sends a non-numeric string; consider catching with try/except and returning 400. Low priority — frontend always sends a number.
payments.py: `users < 1` is clamped to 1 server-side (good). Same clamping is present in ChoosePlan.js stepper (good).

success_rate.frontend: Code-review verified; UI interaction test blocked by flaky login — not a product bug

seed_data_creation: Each test run creates pending payment_transactions rows for the session user — these are expected artefacts (pending, not paid).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend regression file /app/backend/tests/test_enterprise_pricing.py covers the whole Enterprise per-user flow. For Playwright UI tests: on the /auth page you must (1) click [data-testid="auth-email-btn"] first, then (2) fill [data-testid="auth-email-input"] / [data-testid="auth-password-input"] and click [data-testid="auth-submit-btn"]. The form may not render immediately — wait ~1.5s after click. Note: /choose-plan requires auth and will redirect to / when unauthenticated. Useful data-testids already in code: plan-card-enterprise, plan-card-pro, plan-card-essential, enterprise-users-minus/plus/count, toggle-monthly, toggle-yearly, pay-now-btn. Verified frontend calculations via code review: 5→$1,300, 7→$1,820, 10→$2,600 monthly; yearly 5→$10,920 (original $15,600 line-through). Backend POST /api/payments/create-checkout with {plan, origin_url, users} confirmed to store amount=plan.price*users when per_user=True.
rca_of_the_issue: No bugs found. Enterprise per-user pricing is implemented correctly across backend (quantity=users when per_user=True, final_price=plan.price*quantity, stored in payment_transactions.amount) and frontend (ChoosePlan stepper updates displayed totals and passes ?users=N to Checkout; Checkout multiplies price*userCount and renders '$X × N users' + correct Pay button amount).
